sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Rakesh Kumar Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Shatrunjay Singh
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
2. Heard Sri Rakesh Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for applicant and Sri Shatrunjay Singh, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri R.P. Patel, learned State Law Officer for the State.

3. The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No.92 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B, 323, 504 and 506 IPC and Sections 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Haldi, District Ballia with the prayer to enlarge her on bail.
4. The FIR was instituted by the informant stating that his sister was married to the co-accused person Rakesh Kumar Singh as per Hindu rites on 14.11.2021.

There are general allegations against Anjali Devi vs State Of U.P. on 3 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142531563/
1 all the accused persons of having demanded dowry from her and subjected her to cruelty and thereafter beaten her on 20.04.2024 and had left her at matimonial home.

entities.text: Anjali Devi vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The sister of the informant was grievously hurt, as such, she was admitted to the hospital, whereby she succumbed to injuries.
5. Learned counsel has stated that the applicant is the sister-in-law (jethani) of the deceased and has nothing to do with the said offence.
She has been falsely implicated in the present case owing to her relationship with the named accused person.

No particular role has been assigned to the applicant,
as such, she is entitled for bail.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against her.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 29.04.2024, having no criminal history to his credit, deserves to be released on bail.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, she will not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with trial.

6. Per contra, learned State Law Officer and learned counsel for the informant have vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the statement of the deceased person was recorded by the Investigating Officer and it is in the vernacular language of the deceased which categorically indicates that all the accused persons had beaten her up and she was delirious at the time of recording of her statement and it indicates that all the accused persons had assaulted her.
The injuries are on the vital part of the body of the victim.

The said statement tentamount to dying declaration, as such, the applicant is not entitled for bail.
7.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the said statement of the deceased person recorded by the Investigating Officer, I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.
8. The bail application is found devoid of merits and is, accordingly, rejected.

9. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously as early as possible in view of the principle as has been laid down in the recent judgments of the Apex Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab; 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India; (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.
